chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who rebukes a believer with a sin will not die until he commits it.

key_terms.عَيَّرَ: to rebuke or remind of a fault

ai.seo_question: What happens to the person who reminds a believer of their sin?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from al-Kafi is interpreted as a divine guarantee of retribution, where the specific sin highlighted becomes the individual's spiritual downfall. It underscores the principle of 'tadhiyyah' (reminding of faults) as a distinct ethical violation that invites a corresponding fate, reinforcing the importance of modesty in correcting others.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who rebukes a Momin with a sin would not die until he commits it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
Whoever debases a believer for a sin will not die before he himself commits such a sin.’”
